newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM cancels trip to continue cabinet talks.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM cancels trip to continue cabinet talks.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has cancelled a planned trip to the Netherlands on Wednesday to continue talks with his partners in the centre-right ruling coalition on restructuring the cabinet, Klaus's office said.

The leaders of the three coalition parties ended a morning meeting and were to report to their individual party leaderships about the state of the coalition talks, government spokesman Ivo Strejcek told journalists. Klaus was scheduled to attend a ceremony marking the 50th anniversary of the Marshall plan in the Hague.
The government has also cancelled its regular Wednesday meeting, Strejcek said.

Coalition leaders agreed last week to make changes in the cabinet amid a sharp drop in the government's approval rating spurred by an economic downturn and numerous reports of financial crimes and banking failures.

Leaders on Tuesday evening began discussing a declaration on the government programme which would accompany the changes. The Czech news agency CTK said overnight meetings of the junior coalition parties revealed a major split in opinions on the declaration.

It quoted Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) chairman Michael Zantovsky as flatly rejecting a proposal by the Christian Democrats to initiate import restrictions to relieve a massive trade deficit which has put pressure on the crown.
